newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ACTIVE OPTIONS TRADE FOCUSES ON LONG-TERM CALLS.
newsitem.headline: ACTIVE OPTIONS TRADE FOCUSES ON LONG-TERM CALLS.

text.p: Hansapank stock options trading snapped out of a period of inactivity last week with a healthly volume of 40 million kroons as investors chased long-term calls, Hanspank said on Monday.
"December and November calls in banking stocks were the most active during the short three-day week," Tonis Haavel, Hansapank's options trader, told Reuters.
"There was almost no interest in short puts," he added.
Following the general trend, calls based on predictions of a rising bourse in autumn still dominated trade.
"Investors are still expecting a repeat of last year's autumn rise," he added.
With almost no trade in puts, December Talse 270 calls were 35 kroons and September 270 calls were at 21.50 kroons.
December Hansapank 150 calls were at 22.8 kroons, while three-month September 145 calls were at 25 kroons.
Hoiupank's December 150 calls were at 24.9 kroons and three-month calls 150 were 14 kroons.
Norma's December 75 calls were 10.9 kroons and September 75 calls were 5.4 kroons.
The maturity date for options is the third Friday of each month.
Both Hansapank and Tallinna Pank actively trade stock options.
The Tallinn bourse said earlier on Monday that it planned to launch trade in stock options in 1998. --David Mardiste, Tallinn newsroom +372 620 9202 reuters@reuters.ee
